```{r}
#| label: answers
#| include: false
# Computes every number quoted in the answer boxes, so they always match the
# data. Students never see this chunk.
suppressMessages({
  library(sf)
  library(dplyr)
  library(readr)
})
shp <- "data/9-1-co-counties.shp"
co_raw <- st_read(shp, quiet = TRUE)
n_co <- nrow(co_raw)
crs_raw <- st_crs(co_raw)$input
bb_raw <- round(st_bbox(co_raw), 1)
sqdeg <- round(sum(st_area(co_raw)), 1)

co <- st_set_crs(co_raw, 4269)
area_km2 <- units::set_units(st_area(co), km^2)
total_km2 <- round(sum(as.numeric(area_km2)))
largest <- co$name[which.max(area_km2)]
largest_km2 <- round(max(as.numeric(area_km2)))
smallest <- co$name[which.min(area_km2)]
smallest_km2 <- round(min(as.numeric(area_km2)))

st_tab <- read_csv("data/9-1-stations.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
n_st <- nrow(st_tab)
st <- st_as_sf(st_tab, coords = c("easting", "northing"), crs = 26913)
bb_st <- round(st_bbox(st))
bb_st_ll <- round(st_bbox(st_transform(st, 4269)), 1)
inside <- sum(lengths(st_intersects(st_transform(st, 4269), co)) > 0)

# Maria's code
maria_st <- st_as_sf(read.csv("data/9-1-stations.csv"), coords = c("northing", "easting"), crs = 4269)
bb_maria <- round(st_bbox(maria_st))
maria_area <- as.numeric(st_area(co_raw)) / 1e6
maria_max <- format(signif(max(maria_area), 2), scientific = FALSE)

# Round trip
gpkg <- file.path(tempdir(), "co.gpkg")
st_write(co, gpkg, delete_dsn = TRUE, quiet = TRUE)
back <- st_read(gpkg, quiet = TRUE)
```

This is an in-class exercise. Before class, work through the lecture **09-1: Spatial Data and Vector Layers**. In class, you work through the worksheet with an AI assistant writing the code. Your job is everything the AI cannot do: finding out what the coordinates mean, asking for the right thing and the right checks, and judging whether the result is right.

# Setup {#sec-setup}

1. Download the worksheet, [ex-9-1.qmd](worksheets/ex-9-1.qmd), and the data files:
   + [9-1-co-counties.shp](data/9-1-co-counties.shp), [9-1-co-counties.shx](data/9-1-co-counties.shx) and [9-1-co-counties.dbf](data/9-1-co-counties.dbf) (three files, one layer)
   + [9-1-stations.csv](data/9-1-stations.csv)
   + [9-1-README.txt](data/9-1-README.txt)
2. Make an R Project folder called `ch9-practice`, with two subfolders, `data` and `analysis`. You may ask the AI how to do this.
3. Copy the five data files into `ch9-practice/data`, and the worksheet into `ch9-practice/analysis`.
4. Ask the AI to install the `sf` package if you have not already.
5. Open the worksheet and start at Task 1.

::: {.callout-important title="It worked if"}
Typing `here::here()` in the Console prints the path to `ch9-practice` and nothing longer.

If `here::here()` prints a path ending in `analysis`, the `.Rproj` file was not recognised. `here` only accepts a `.Rproj` file whose first line starts with `Version:`, which every project created in RStudio (File, New Project) has.
:::

# Answers {#sec-answers}

Open each one only after you have tried the task.

## Task 1: Look and predict

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="What you should find"}
A. The counties: longitude and latitude in NAD83, EPSG 4269. The stations: metres in NAD83 / UTM zone 13N, EPSG 26913.

B. The `.prj` file is missing, and the README says so. That file holds the CRS, so the layer will be read with no CRS at all.

C. `r n_st` stations. `easting` holds x and `northing` holds y. Values such as `r format(st_tab$easting[1], big.mark = ",")` and `r format(st_tab$northing[1], big.mark = ",")` are metres, not degrees, which agrees with the README.

D. Colorado runs from about -109 to -102 longitude and 37 to 41 latitude, and its area is about 270,000 square kilometres (104,000 square miles). Any map site or encyclopedia gives these.
:::

## Task 2: Read the counties

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="What you should find"}
`r n_co` features of type `MULTIPOLYGON`, and a bounding box from `r bb_raw["xmin"]` to `r bb_raw["xmax"]` in x and `r bb_raw["ymin"]` to `r bb_raw["ymax"]` in y, which is where Colorado is. The quick map looks like Colorado.

The CRS check fails: expected EPSG 4269, got `NA` (no CRS). Everything else passes, which is the point: the layer looks right on a map and has the right numbers in it. Only the CRS check says that R does not know what those numbers mean.

The blanks of the request, filled in:

```text
In my R project, data/9-1-co-counties.shp is a shapefile (.shp) file with one
row per county. Its documentation says the CRS is NAD83, EPSG 4269.
...
the number of features (I expect 64), the geometry type (I expect
MULTIPOLYGON), and the bounding box (I expect longitude between -109
and -102 and latitude between 37 and 41).
```
:::

## Task 3: Fix the CRS, then compute areas

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="What you should find"}
**Prediction without the fix.** With no CRS, `st_area()` treats the numbers as plain x and y and returns square degrees: the counties add up to `r sqdeg`, with no units and no warning.

**After labelling the layer with EPSG 4269** (`st_set_crs()`, not `st_transform()`, because the numbers are already right and only the label is missing): the CRS check passes and the bounding box is unchanged.

**Areas.** The counties add up to `r format(total_km2, big.mark = ",")` square kilometres, against about 270,000 from the encyclopedia: the check passes. The largest county is `r largest` (`r format(largest_km2, big.mark = ",")` km²) and the smallest is `r smallest` (`r format(smallest_km2, big.mark = ",")` km²).

If the AI used `st_transform()` instead of `st_set_crs()`, it stops with an error, because a layer with no CRS cannot be transformed: there is nothing to transform from. That error is the good case.
:::

## Task 4: The stations

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="What you should find"}
`r n_st` features, CRS EPSG 26913. The bounding box in the layer's own CRS runs from `r format(bb_st["xmin"], big.mark = ",")` to `r format(bb_st["xmax"], big.mark = ",")` metres in x: you cannot compare that with a map. Transformed to EPSG 4269, it runs from `r bb_st_ll["xmin"]` to `r bb_st_ll["xmax"]` longitude and `r bb_st_ll["ymin"]` to `r bb_st_ll["ymax"]` latitude, inside Colorado.

**The check from knowing the place:** `r inside` of `r n_st` stations fall inside a Colorado county. The counting needs both layers in one CRS: the AI should transform the stations to the counties' CRS (or the other way) first. If it does not, `sf` stops with the error `st_crs(x) == st_crs(y) is not TRUE`.

On the map, every point should sit inside the state outline. If the points form a tiny cluster far from Colorado, or the map's axes run into the hundreds of thousands, one layer was given the wrong CRS.
:::

## Task 5: Maria's code

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answers"}
A. Line 1 reads the county shapefile. Line 2 reads the stations csv and makes it a layer of points, with `northing` as x, `easting` as y, labelled as longitude and latitude in NAD83. Line 3 adds each county's area, divided by a million.

B. The paths. `C:/Users/maria/Downloads` exists only on Maria's computer.

C. Three problems, none of which gives an error:

1. Line 2 swaps x and y.
2. Line 2 labels metres as degrees (EPSG 4269 instead of 26913). The layer's bounding box runs from `r format(bb_maria["xmin"], big.mark = ",")` to `r format(bb_maria["xmax"], big.mark = ",")` in x, numbers no longitude can have.
3. The counties have no CRS (no `.prj`), so line 3 computes square degrees and divides them by a million. The largest "area" is `r maria_max`.

D. The bounding box catches problems 1 and 2. The CRS check catches the missing CRS behind problem 3, and the total area against Colorado's known area catches the result.

E. The AI usually spots the paths and often the swapped coordinates, since `northing` as x is visible in the code. It cannot know that the counties file has no `.prj` or that the stations are in metres, because it has not seen the files. Compare its list with yours.
:::

## Task 6: Save and read back

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="What you should find"}
The GeoPackage comes back with EPSG `r st_crs(back)$epsg`, `r nrow(back)` features and the same columns: the check passes. A `.gpkg` is one file that keeps its CRS, so the problem you met in Task 2, a shapefile that lost its `.prj`, cannot happen to it.
:::
